summary: A lookout hill light off the Maine coast since 1824, kept for decades by Betsey Humphrey after her husband died; the keeper's house is now a museum.

access.note: Museum in keeper's house open mid-June to end September; tower tours scheduled; island reached by ferry.

notes_for_editor: Mostly secondary (Lighthouse Friends) for people and dates; no newspaper or pre-1891 primary source was read, and the Albee letter and 1850 tower details are second-hand via Lighthouse Friends. Tower height conflict: NRHP 47 ft vs LF 38 ft (first tower) and 30 ft (1850 tower, apparently inconsistent). Lens year 1856 (USLHS) vs 1857 (LF). Museum page says tower tours; LF says tower closed. 1891-92 volume covers two fiscal years; printed pages not confirmed (cited by volume). Roster stints taken from USLHS; Manana fog-signal keepers not listed. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Albee letter dated 'after a year at the light' (not 1841) per Lighthouse Friends; LF gives 30 ft for the 1850 tower, now stated in the story.
